plan: In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' actions, since you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks losses if you win. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid exactly my value of $36 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win only when your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you pay that second-highest bid, ensuring non-negative profit whenever you win. Bidding above value risks paying more than the item is worth; bidding below value risks losing profitable wins. With value $8, bidding exactly $8 guarantees I never overpay and capture all profitable opportunities.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win exactly when your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you pay that second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you're highest). Bidding below value risks losing profitable wins; bidding above value risks negative profit. With value $44, the optimal bid is $44, ensuring maximum expected profit given uniform value distribution among competitors.
